about: #27's budgets (AC3), with the numbers the owner approved on 2026-10-31 from docs/performance/baseline-1.4.0.md. No script writes this file: it changes only by review, and a number over a row goes back to the owner through the lead, never raised by the lane. docs/performance/budgets.md says how each gate runs and what fails it.

reference.about: The frozen package the timing and heap runs measure against, twice a round: v1.4.0 built with its own lockfile and build (npm run perf:reference). The digest is a SHA-256 over its files sorted by path (scripts/perf-probe.js packageDigest), and npm run perf:probe --baseline refuses a run whose first or second package isn't it.

timing.rule: Paired and interleaved: each run times the frozen 1.4.0 package twice and the candidate once a round, rotated, at least 12 rounds per profile and a multiple of the package count. It fails when the candidate's median ratio to the mean of the two 1.4.0 runs is over 1 + tolerancePct / 100, and it's invalid when 1.4.0 against itself is more than tolerancePct off. Absolute ms are recorded beside it, not gated.
timing.modeAbout: gate since 2026-10-31, under the rule it reported by until then: gate after 10 CI runs if 1.4.0 against itself stayed within 7% on at least 9 and the invalid-run check would have passed. The perf workflow ran on 14 pushes to next, f7a17e5e to 7489d7b3, and all 14 were valid: the worst 1.4.0-against-itself median was +2.6% on typical and -2.2% on maximal. A timing fail, or an invalid run, now fails CI's perf job. The perf job isn't in pr-gate's needs or any ruleset, so it blocks no merge; making it block one is the owner's call (docs/performance/budgets.md).

heap.modeAbout: gate since 2026-11-01, at today's heap plus about 5%, the rule the owner approved for the byte rows; the coordinator decided it for the owner, who can reverse it. CI's 1.4.0 heap (3.94 to 3.98 MiB over 14 runs on next) matches the Mac's (3.94 to 4.01) within about 1%, so a MiB number means the same on both. The candidate measured 2.68 MiB on typical and 2.56 on maximal on 7489d7b3 (perf run 41280346766): 2.68 x 1.05 is 2.81, failing above 2.89 with the 3%. One number gates both profiles, so maximal has more room. The 4.45 MiB row it replaces was next's heap on the Mac before slice 3, 66% above today. A heap fail, or an invalid run, fails CI's perf job, which isn't in pr-gate's needs or any ruleset, so it blocks no merge.

model-runtime.about: transformers.js. The package ships no .wasm, and the analyzer lists only chunks, classic scripts, stylesheets and fonts, so a .wasm path here would guard nothing: one gets a path with the analyzer support to see it

archive-trash.about: archive and trash administration, which has no module of its own until #3 splits it out of the sidebar

ai-policy.about: #21's AI scope and destination policy, none yet

workspace.about: the workspace chunk and every Workspace route

newtab.reason: The new tab. Until #2 builds Moment, the workspace chunk is the whole tab and loads at boot, so it counts as start (#27 slice 3). Its forbidden list is what's enforceable today: the four libraries and the trust code, which slice 3 made lazy. The full list waits for the moment row.

popup.reason: The Popup's start JS. Its CSS and HTML have no approved numbers yet, and its timing and heap wait for #4's ready mark.

sidepanel.reason: The Side Panel's start JS. Its CSS and HTML have no approved numbers yet, and its timing and heap wait for #5's ready mark.

offscreen.reason: The offscreen document, which runs AI requests for the service worker. Its rows are today's size plus about 5%, decided for the owner on 2026-11-01: on 7489d7b3 its start JS was 28,150 / 8,818 bytes (the page's module and js/network-guard.js) and its HTML 230 / 174. The HTML row is 1 KiB, the smallest round row, since 5% of 230 bytes is 12. It loads no stylesheet, and no fonts.

background.reason: The service worker. Its cold-start time is #35's, and stays null until #35 sets it; its graph is one self-contained module (#27 slice 2), and its third-party packages are checked like a page's.

moment.reason: #2's Moment, a loader chunk the new tab will boot instead of the workspace. The full forbidden list holds from its first build. Its numbers come from the owner before #2 builds it: a built planned row fails (AC3).
